title: Finite-clopen detection of constructibility and fixed cohomological and Tor bounds
statement:
Fix the global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$, $i\in I$, be a finite pairwise disjoint open and closed cover [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-pur-conventions].

Put $A=A_{E,n}$ for $n\ge1$ and let $r_i$ be derived restriction on $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-tensor]. A sheaf $F$ of $A$-modules is constructible in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] if and only if every $F|_{X_i}$ is constructible. More precisely, restriction of a finite locally closed constructibility stratification intersects its strata with $X_i$; conversely the component strata, viewed as subschemes of $X$, form a finite constructibility stratification with the same locally constant finite-module models.

For any $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and any integers $a\le b$, its cohomology vanishes outside $[a,b]$ if and only if the cohomology of every $r_iK$ does. The cohomology sheaves of $K$ are constructible if and only if those of every $r_iK$ are. Tor amplitude in the fixed interval $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] is equivalent to Tor amplitude in that same interval on every component: the test objects are all module sheaves in degree zero, including those obtained by zero insertion from a single component.

Consequently the unbounded restriction equivalence restricts to equivalences on $D^b_c(-,A)$ and $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Any common cohomological bounds, and any common Tor bounds, for the finitely many component complexes are bounds for the glued complex. Empty components and $I=\varnothing$ are allowed, and the zero object satisfies every such interval condition.

proof.text: First check the strata as subschemes, not only as point sets. Each clopen $X_i$ is retrocompact in $X$: its intersection with a quasi-compact open $W$ is closed in $W$, hence quasi-compact. A constructible stratum $S\subset X$ restricts to a constructible subset of $X_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-open-restriction]. Write its immersion as a closed immersion $S\hookrightarrow V$ followed by an open immersion $V\hookrightarrow X$. Base change along $X_i\hookrightarrow X$ gives a closed immersion $S\times_X X_i\hookrightarrow V\times_X X_i$ and an open immersion $V\times_X X_i\hookrightarrow X_i$ by the two cited base-change lemmas. Thus the restricted stratum is an actual locally closed subscheme. Conversely, a stratum $T\hookrightarrow X_i$ factors as $T\hookrightarrow V\hookrightarrow X_i$ with the first arrow closed and the second open. The same $V$ is open in $X$ (the open subsets and restricted structure sheaves agree), so this is a locally closed immersion into $X$. Its image is constructible in $X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-image-retrocompact-open], since $X_i$ is retrocompact open. These constructions retain the original subscheme structures.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] with $R=A_X$. It identifies $R|_{X_i}$ with $A_{X_i}$ and gives the exact module restriction equivalence with zero insertions $e_i$. In particular a module sheaf is zero if all its restrictions are zero: under the displayed quasi-inverse its sections are the product of zero modules. By [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus], degreewise restriction induces the unbounded derived equivalence and $H^m(r_iK)\cong r_iH^m(K)$ for every integer $m$. Consequently $H^m(K)=0$ iff every $H^m(r_iK)=0$. Apply this separately for each $m\notin[a,b]$ to get precisely the claimed fixed cohomological interval. Apply the sheaf equivalence established in steps 2 and 3 to each $H^m(K)$ to get the assertion about constructible cohomology.

proof.text:
Assume all $r_iK$ have Tor amplitude in the same $[a,b]$. Let $M$ be any $A_X$-module sheaf in degree zero. The tensor comparison of [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus] identifies
$$r_i(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M)\cong r_iK\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}r_iM.$$
Exact degreewise restriction leaves $r_iM$ in degree zero. The right side therefore has zero cohomology outside $[a,b]$ by the component Tor hypothesis and [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. For every $m\notin[a,b]$, step 4 detects the vanishing of $H^m(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M)$ from these component vanishings. Since $M$ was arbitrary, this is exactly Tor amplitude of $K$ in $[a,b]$.

proof.text:
Assume instead that $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Fix $i$ and any $A_{X_i}$-module sheaf $N$ in degree zero. Use the module zero insertion $M=e_iN$ from [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing], also placed in degree zero. Its $i$th restriction is $N$, and its other restrictions are zero. The global Tor hypothesis says $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$. Restricting this complex and using the cohomology and tensor comparisons of [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus] gives
$$r_i(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}e_iN)\cong r_iK\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N,$$
again concentrated in $[a,b]$. Because every $N$ was permitted, [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] gives the required Tor interval for $r_iK$. This proves the other implication without assuming that an arbitrary component test object was originally the restriction of a globally given one.

proof.text: The equivalence of [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus] is fully faithful on all objects and essentially surjective on tuples. By step 4 and [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], a complex is bounded constructible exactly when all its component complexes are: in the reverse direction choose component cohomological intervals $[c_i,d_i]$ and, for nonempty finite $I$, use $c=\min_i c_i$, $d=\max_i d_i$. Vanishing outside $[c_i,d_i]$ implies vanishing outside $[c,d]$, so step 4 applies to any inverse image of the tuple. Likewise, for a tuple in $D^b_{ctf}$, choose component Tor intervals $[u_i,v_i]$ as in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], enlarge them to $[\min_i u_i,\max_i v_i]$, and apply step 5. Step 6 proves preservation in the forward direction. Thus this equivalence restricts to both asserted full subcategories. The same argument uses any preassigned common cohomological or Tor interval, proving the final assertion about bounds, not just the existence of some bounds.

proof.text: The empty cases require no minimum or maximum. Empty components have zero module categories by [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] and zero derived categories by [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus]. If $I$ is empty the covering condition forces $X$ empty, so the unique derived object is zero. The zero sheaf is locally constant with the finite zero module as its model, hence constructible by [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]; on the empty scheme one can use the empty stratification. Its cohomology in every degree is zero. Tensoring its zero complex with any complex gives the zero complex, so [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] holds for every interval $[a,b]$. Thus all the assertions, including the subcategory equivalences and arbitrary common bounds, hold also for empty $X$, empty $I$, and covers containing empty components.
